newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish markets to sail calmer waters next week.
newsitem.headline: Polish markets to sail calmer waters next week.

text.p: The Polish money market hopes to regain liquidity next week after a severe cash shortage pulled one-day rates up five percentage points this week to highs around the 25 percent lombard rate, analysts said on Friday.
They said, however, that waters may still get choppy for banks as they adjust monthly required reserve levels next week -- the last in September's reserve account ending next Sunday.
"The focus will be on balancing reserve levels next week but (one-day) rates should be much more calm than this week," said Wladyslaw Kado, money market dealer at Bank Handlowy SA. @

The market's cash-shortage, caused by banks overinvesting in central bank drainage operations earlier in the month, pulled call-money rates to just below 25 percent from 19.13 percent -- the market's main 14-day reverse repo rate.
Analysts said the end of the reserve should keep overnight rates from falling below the 14-day drainage rate level next week after Friday's close at around 18.80/20.10 percent.
"Rates will still be high but should not top 20.5 percent next week as a lot of cash returns and banks build up reserves over the weekend," said Violetta Gorecka, dealer at PKO SA. @

Analysts expected the average yield of the 52-week T-bill to hold flat around 19.46 percent at Monday's primary auction, but said the 8-week bill yield would likely fall under the weight of non-banking sector bids.
"The longer paper should remain basically flat on Monday, while the shorter one is in the domain of client bids and may fall," said Rafal Chodzidlo, senior dealer at Bank Slaski SA.
Analysts said the 8-week paper yield may fall to between 18.40 and 18.50 from an average yield of 18.63 percent at the last auction at which it was offered on August 26. @
They said demand should be around 900 million zlotys against the treasury's 500 million offer, comprised of 400 million 52-week bills and 100 million of the 8-week paper.

The zloty is expected to remain within a tight band between 1.6-1.8 percent from the parity rate next week after rising to a high of 1.93 percent this week as banks shortened foreign currency positions to take advantage of high deposit rates.
"We expect a quiet week as there doesn't seem to be much pressure on the zloty to either strenghten or weaken," said Jan Mieczkowski, treasurer at Deutsche Bank Polska SA. @
The zloty closed the week at 2.7930 to the dollar and at 1.8415 to the mark, or about 1.78 percent from the parity rate.
